title: Helping Men Recover
official: Helping Men Recover (HMR): A Program for Treating Addiction
summary:
The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of the Helping Men Recover (HMR) curriculum at California State Prison-Corcoran. The HMR program to be evaluated utilizes a Peer-Facilitated model of implementation (i.e., residents serving life or long sentences will be trained to facilitate the delivery of the HMR program to other residents). The peer-facilitated program is delivered over 21 sessions and utilizes a Facilitator Guide and Participant Workbook. This evaluation study will employ a randomized experimental design; the most rigorous design that can be employed in evaluation research.

The program is delivered by trained peer facilitators in general institutional housing on a custody level III yard. Researchers assess changes in trauma-related distress, behavioral health symptoms, anger, and aggression using validated self-report measures administered before and after the intervention period.

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* All participants who expressed interest in participating in the study at the California men's prison
* All who were capable of providing written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

\- There were no study-defined exclusion criteria; operational exclusions or security restrictions were at the discretion of prison administration.
